The remaining nulls are filled by rule, never by choice: the two reference rates from five native arms at T=10 per workload (D-14 §2; a dated amendment), and the fork revision when the Programme 1 binary is built. authority.decisions: docs/PREREGISTRATION.md D-13, as amended by D-14 and D-15

replaces.reason: Programme 1 replaces the constrained objective with a priced cost. The 2026-09-11 programme's record stays in PREREGISTRATION section 4 and in git history.

objective.form: priced cost J_beta, PATHWAYS D section 2

prices.price_per_core_second_rule: instance_price_per_second / instance_cores: every priced operation runs on one thread and occupies one core (D-15 §3a)
prices.instance_price_source: AWS us-east-1 on-demand, m8a.4xlarge, $0.974 per hour (16 physical Zen 5 cores, 64 GiB), retrieved 2026-09-30; closest public match to Chameleon compute_zen5_grado
prices.storage_price_source: AWS us-east-1 EBS gp3, $0.08 per GB-month, GB = 1e9 bytes, month = 730 hours, retrieved 2026-09-30
prices.device_times: c_w, c_f, c_blk and c_sk are core-seconds per unit, times price_per_core_second, measured on the node by 18_calibrate_prices as D-15 §3 fixes: c_w from the q-bar native arms' own flush and compaction jobs, the read prices as marginal times from slopes across trees at T = 2, 6 and 10; median of five repeats (reads) or of the q-bar runs (writes)

reference_rate.rule: mean measured-phase throughput (n_w to the end of mixgraph) of five native arms at T=10 per workload, run through 03 with the settle step at the Gate N2 run length on the Programme 1 binary, frozen before any static-class run (D-14 §2, superseding D-13 §1's ACT-4 repeats)

write_accounting: Lemma D.7's exact identity with the overlap constant measured per level; replaces P0-7's M3 convention

workloads.assoc: PREREGISTRATION D-1 unchanged: keyrange_num 30, delete rate 0

powerlaw_get95.label: YCSB-B operation mix with power-law key popularity; never Zipfian or YCSB-B

profiles.survival_weighted: Theorem A.2(ii): f_i = lambda / v_i with v_i = a_i - t_i measured over mixgraph (n_w to drain_start) on the native arms of the same (workload, T, K0, base size) point, L and B_L from the settled tree at n_w; c_i measured and reported; entries clipped to [0.5, 2.0]; computed by 23_static_profiles.py (D-14 §3)

last_level_emptying.level: the level just above the deepest populated level of the native arms of the same (workload, T, K0, base size) point, on their settled tree at n_w (D-14 §3)

cross_t_check.configuration: each mode's theta_star at T=10, per workload

repeats.top_up: smallest n with n >= (t_{0.975,n-1} sigma_d / h)^2, h a quarter of the J_beta gap between theta_star and the next-best static point, per workload, T and mode

measured_phase.settle: after the bulk load, a db_bench settle step calls WaitForCompact with flushes included, then holds while every level's score stays below 1 and L0 files stay below the trigger

stall_rule.stall_fraction: measured-phase stall seconds / mixgraph wall time (measure_start to drain_start stamps; D-14 §1)
stall_rule.stall_seconds_source: internal-stats Cumulative stall line differenced over the measured phase (D-11); never rocksdb.stall.micros
stall_rule.bounds: the ends of the two-sided 95% paired Student-t interval (pipeline_stats.ci95): the stall bound is its upper end and the throughput bound its lower end, each a one-sided 97.5% bound (D-15 §1)

build.mechanism: RocksDB PORTABLE cache variable; PORTABLE=0 would emit -march=native
build.why_not_native: native silently degrades to a generic microarchitecture on a compiler that does not know the host CPU
build.measurement_node: single-socket AMD EPYC 4545P, 16 cores, SMT off, one NUMA node

io.amended: 2026-09-12, in place, before any Gate 1 run
io.reason: pinned off on measured cost. On the measurement node at 10M T=2, mixgraph ran at 2750 ops/s with direct I/O and 58332 ops/s buffered, a 21x penalty putting the Gate 1 sweep near 95 hours.
io.consequence: the host page cache holds the database, so latency, runtime and stall figures are warm-cache and are reported as such. They bound foreground disruption; they are not storage latency claims.
io.revisit: may be set true for the final paper benchmark workload if the amplification results justify the cost. Such runs carry fingerprint field dio1, cannot be pooled with dio0 runs, and need their own comparator manifest because stage 06 selects on runtime, which is cache-sensitive.
io.rejected_alternative: a cgroup memory cap on the benchmark process. It is external state the fingerprint cannot carry and a new lease silently loses.

measured.node: AMD EPYC 4545P, buffered vs direct, 10M T=2 mixgraph

io.correction: an earlier revision of this entry quoted a 2.6x penalty. That compared the direct-I/O pilot on this node against a buffered figure from the 2026-09-03 suite, which ran on different hardware. The cross-machine comparison was invalid; the same-node penalty is 21x. Recorded rather than silently replaced.

measurement_environment.cpu_pinning: db_bench and the Python controller run on disjoint cores that share no last-level cache
measurement_environment.note: recorded for provenance; a differently pinned arm is not yet refused by the paired evaluator

amendments.reason: before any governed run: the stall fraction's time base is mixgraph's wall time (the literal measured-phase base rewarded deferral into the drain); q-bar is measured by native arms at T=10, since ACT-4 runs at T=2; the survival-weighted profile's computation is fixed

before any governed run and before any price was measured: prices per core-second instead of per whole-machine second (a one-thread operation was charged 16 cores against c_s); the measurement method of the device prices; the stall rule's bounds read as the ends of the two-sided 95% interval; CMP-7's competitor set

suite_robustness.competitors: static configurations run with the same setting on every workload (same fingerprint without the workload's own segments; 07 config_key)
suite_robustness.excluded: the survival-weighted and last-level-emptying profiles, computed per workload, unless a vector is identical on every workload; they stay in theta_star(w), so every regret is against the whole class
suite_robustness.consequence: the min-max can only rise, so CMP-7 is easier for the controller than over the whole class; stated beside every CMP-7 result, with the excluded configurations listed
